title: History
tagline: Learn how the past made the present, and how to find the truth about it in the evidence.
overview:
The Certificate in History is a three-year course of study in the human past and the craft of understanding it. You begin with how historians work and with surveys of world, United States, and regional history, then deepen your knowledge of the forces that shaped the modern world: revolution, empire, industrialization, war, and decolonization.

Along the way you learn to read primary sources, weigh competing interpretations, and build arguments from evidence. In your final year you choose a concentration in American, European, or global and comparative history, and complete a two-term senior thesis based on original research.
outcomes: Explain major developments in world, regional, and United States history and the connections among them.
Analyze primary sources critically, attending to authorship, audience, context, and reliability.
Evaluate competing historical interpretations and the evidence behind them.
Design and carry out original historical research.
Write clear, persuasive, evidence-based historical arguments.
Explain how societies remember and use the past, and why it matters.

careers.title: Research and Writing
careers.description: Investigate questions and write clearly for publishers, media, policy groups, and businesses.

careers.title: Teaching
careers.description: Bring history to life for students in schools and community programs.

careers.title: Graduate Study
careers.description: Prepare for graduate work in history, law, library science, or public policy.
